column1: # Step 1 (01-spark-30): what each scored family is worth.
# Since 2026-10-13 (user decision, product scoring) the two families are
# multiplied, not added: reward = T1 x T2, where T1 is the migrated family's
# points over its total weight below and T2 is the behavior family's points
# over its total weight below (score.py, product_reward). The weights still
# sum to 1; they now set the proportions inside each factor. Where the prose
# below speaks of a family's share of the reward, read it as that family's
# share before this change.
# Two families, as rule 5 requires, and neither below ~30%:
#   behavior   0.30   the tree still does what it did      replay + the repo's own tests
#   migrated   0.70   the tree is on Scala 2.12 / Spark 3.0.3, off the APIs 3.0
#                     removed, pinned and reproducible
# The split is the step's floor, and the floor is zero. Rule 5's sentence -- the
# untouched previous-step tree passes the first family completely and fails the
# second -- assumes a step in which only the code moves. Here the runtime moves
# with it: all three Spark artifacts are `provided`, so whatever the pom
# resolves, the replay runs the candidate's jar against the /opt/spark 3.0.3 in
# the image. The pin does not pass the behavior family completely; it reproduces
# most of the recordings by accident of compatibility. Paying 0.30 for that
# would make the nop non-zero, which section 8 of migration_prompt.md forbids in
# as many words, so the behavior family is graded only on a build that left the
# 2.4 line at all -- `spark_line_moved` in score.py, read out of the same
# gate/pom.tsv the m1 rules are read from. The pin is red in all six
# requirements (NOTES 6.1.7, 6.1.13) and now scores 0.000000 outright
# The condition is a floor, not a scale. One org.apache.spark artifact resolving
# anywhere off 2.4.x satisfies it, so a candidate who landed on the wrong 3.x,
# or who left a stray 2.4 artifact in a mixed graph, keeps every point of
# proportional behavior credit and loses only the m1 rules that measure those
# things. Nobody who tried falls off a cliff here.
# And -- unlike at the rung this step replaced -- there is no pom-only candidate
# at all. A tree whose pom names Scala 2.12 and Spark 3.0.3 and nothing else
# does not compile: `org.spark_project.guava` is gone,
# `Word2VecModel.Word2VecModelReader` is not accessible, and `spark-xml_2.11`
# has no 2.12 release to resolve. A build that does not build answers neither
# family.
# Within `migrated`, a requirement scores all or nothing: every rule carrying
# its prefix must be PASS. Half a dependency graph is not half migrated, and a
# partial credit there would pay for a pom that names Scala 2.12 while still
# resolving 2.11 through spark-mllib.
# Why m3 is the largest single requirement. It is the one that cannot be
# answered from the build's description of itself: its four rules are read out
# of the constant pools of the classes the build produced, not out of the pom,
# and answering them means editing Java in two files and knowing why. m1 is
# larger than m2 because it is the version move proper; m6 is larger than m4
# because reproducibility costs a plugin upgrade and a build-output change
# rather than a list of versions.
# Within `behavior`, credit is proportional and the unit is rule 7's scored
# input -- 247 of them at this census, 42.9% adversarial (build/inputs.py over
# r23). A demo is one input and its recording is one answer; a harness
# subcommand is as many inputs as it prints labeled cases, and each case's
# block of output is compared on its own so that breaking one of advnumeric's
# 19 costs 1/19 of that job rather than all of it.
# The two behavior weights are in the ratio the two instruments deserve rather
# than in the ratio of their wall-clock: the replay is 247 inputs over 140 jobs
# and the repo's own suite is 142 tests the agent can read and run for itself,
# which rule 7 says counts toward neither bar. It is here because a migration
# that breaks the tree's own tests has broken the tree, not because it measures
# anything the replay does not.
# 37m57s end to end, on 7 vCPU, from this step's first phase header to its
# reward.json: the oracle run of 2026-09-18 (jobs dir m27-s3-oracle, job
# 27-spark24-to-4.0__k7shaVo), taken while another agent's jobs shared the
# box, so it is an upper reading rather than a clean one. Rule 10 aims at
# ~30 minutes a step and caps at 60. The replay opens at 1m35s and the
# inherited suite at 31m28s, so the replay is 30 of the 38 minutes;
# neither the replay's 140 jobs nor the suite's 142 tests is reducible
# without asking a smaller question, and rule 10's own instruction is not
# to shrink a fixture set to fit a clock.
